item.title: GovBrief Today #594
item.description: Congress sent its first Epstein contempt case to Donald Trump's Attorney General on the day a judge warned he could be next. Billionaire investor Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein more than $170 million between 2012 and 2017. He walked out of a closed-door interview with Congress in June and skipped the deposition where members planned to ask what he paid for. Every Republican and Democrat in the House asked the Justice Department to prosecute him. Also Wednesday, a federal judge ruled Todd Blanche is still withholding files the law requires him to release. Blanche has until September 24 to turn over the FBI agents' handwritten notes, including the interview with a woman who told agents Trump and Epstein abused her as a girl. He also has to prove that the names his department blacked out belong to victims. The billionaire's case now lands on the desk of a man facing a contempt countdown of his own. item.title: What I Actually Do When Everyone Leaves
item.description:
Okay, funny video - but the dress actually has a really lovely story When I was in Kauaʻi, I wandered into this little boutique in Hanalei called Inseazen. And sometimes when you're traveling you just randomly meet your people. The woman who owns it and I hit it off almost immediately. We talked and laughed and she was just unbelievably sweet to me. Somewhere in all of that, I ended up in this red dress (and let’s be honest several more of her dresses as well).
And this sounds like such a little thing, but that first picture is one of the most genuinely euphoric photos I've ever taken of myself. There are moments in transition where you catch your reflection and instead of analyzing yourself or looking for what's wrong or wondering how other people see you, your brain just goes: Oh. There I am.
This was one of those. I left Kauaʻi (quite literally) just before the hurricane, but she and I have kept talking since. Now this woman who helped give me such a happy little memory is trying to keep her shop going while Hanalei and the North Shore recover. So I want to return the favor.
So if this silly video got your attention: I'd love to borrow it for something good. Please go show https://www.instagram.com/inseazenkauai/ some love ❤️? Kauaʻi showed me so much love. Just trying to send some back!

item.title: In 2022, Melisa Raouf, became the first Miss England participant to not wear makeup in the pageant’s nearly century-long history.
item.description: "I did not expect my story to spread globally as it has done, but I am delighted that it has, and I hope that it can make a difference to so many women and girls. For so long, I felt as if I was never complete without wearing makeup. Only very recently have I accepted that inner confidence will always shine far more radiantly than any amount of makeup, and doing so has been liberating. Moving forward, I hope to continue promoting #bareface to help empower women of all ages to feel confident in their own skin, without feeling as if they have to conceal their self by wearing makeup in order to conform to societal pressures. Although I do still believe that it is okay to use makeup, we should not let makeup define our appearance. Wearing makeup should not be the default option, but a choice and women should be able to embrace their differences. From the bottom of my heart, I'd like to thank everyone who has supported me through this journey so far. This includes those who donated to my fundraiser for the Beauty with a Purpose charity. The work the charity does with disadvantaged children across the world is so important, particularly at the moment. Through these fundraising efforts, I hope we can really make a positive change for those who need it the most."

item.title: Update on your Local Shrinking Fat Enby
item.description: I have talked some about this on this and my other account I lost access to. But I'll give a recap. Sept 2021 Move to Maine, Significant Lifestyle Changes, lose 80 pounds, Plateau Early 2023 at 420lbs I work a weight loss program for over a year learning and solidifying the new habits Oct 2024 I get gastric sleeve surgery Struggle with overcorrection and under eating Mid 2025- go to the hospital for undereating, nearly die from vitamin deficiency. Get my shit together cause I worked to hard for that. Find a balance, begin exercising more, building muscle. Overall better care of myself. OCT 2025 I hit goal 245 lost since surgery. 325 total. Now in a week I'm getting skin surgery. Panniculectumy/Abdominoplasty. Basically they remove the excess skin in the lower abdomen and do a tummy tuck. I'm terrified. Mostly of the drains. A little of the pain. Infection. Death. Ya...I over think. Yall have been so kind and supportive I just wanted to share where I'm at and if anyone has had a similar surgery and has any advice, please share!!

item.title: Wordy Post for Readers of Theory
item.description:
"After years of colonialism, the Third World country finds it extremely difficult to extricate itself from the unequal relationship with its former colonizer and impossible to depart from the global capitalist sphere. Those countries that try to make a break are subjected to punishing economic and military treatment by one or another major power, nowadays usually the United States. The leaders of the new nations may voice revolutionary slogans, yet they find themselves locked into the global capitalist orbit, cooperating perforce with the First World nations for investment, trade, and aid. So we witnessed the curious phenomenon of leaders of newly independent Third World nations denouncing imperialism as the source of their countries' ills, while dissidents in these countries denounce these same leaders as collaborators of imperialism. In many instances a comprador class emerged or was installed as a first condition for independence. A comprador class is one that cooperates in turning its own country into a client state for foreign interests. A client state is one that is open to investments on terms that are decidedly favorable to the foreign investors. In a client state, corporate investors enjoy direct subsidies and land grants, access to raw materials and cheap labor, light or nonexistent taxes, few effective labor unions, no minimum wage or child labor or occupational safety laws, and no consumer or environmental protections to speak of. The protective laws that do exist go largely unenforced." - Michael Parenti, Against Empire
